message.subject: Using a 20-year-old Windows tool to fix a PC
message.html:
May 22, 2026

We're almost there, folks!

Sometimes the answer requires you to look back in time, and by that, I mean two decades. You'd be forgiven for not being old enough to recall Hiren's BootCD, but this was an invaluable resource in the Windows XP days. Fully kitted out, this compact USB can offer some incredibly useful functionality with a wide range of admin BCD-MBR, storage, network, security, and Windows recovery tools. If you build PCs or sometimes encounter issues, Hiren's BootCD is a tried and tested solution.

Love XDA? We have so much more!

Follow us on Google

This 20-year-old Windows tool fixed my dead PC when nothing else would

By Joe Rice-Jones
May 21, 2026

What if I told you that one of the best rescue tools for Windows PCs was over two decades old? Or that it was filled with Windows fixes, utilities, and apps to get all but the most broken Windows installations running again?

Read More »

I bought the RX 9070 XT for FSR 4, but the games I actually play don't support it

By Ty Sherback
May 21, 2026

When I bought my RX 9070 XT upon release, I expected FSR 4 to be one of the bigger parts of my upgrade. AMD's machine-learning upscaler had been positioned as the answer to DLSS, and the actual gameplay footage that was put out by reviewers backed up the image quality claims.

Read More »

Home Assistant on bare metal works great — until it becomes your entire home's infrastructure

By Rich Edmonds
May 21, 2026

Before combining everything onto a few Proxmox-powered cluster nodes, I ran dedicated hardware for specific packages, be it Home Assistant and Frigate. The former was running on a compact mini PC, and by compact, I mean ridiculously small. It had an Intel chip, barely any RAM, and almost no storage, making it perfect for running the smart home ... or so I thought.

Read More »

I spent weeks chasing a DisplayPort problem that HDMI solved in seconds

By Ty Sherback
May 21, 2026

DisplayPort has largely been the primary cable PC enthusiasts reach for, and for good reason. It has better bandwidth than the HDMI of its era, native VRR before HDMI caught up, and there's no royalty funny business or weird treatment of Linux drivers.

I used frame generation wrong for months - here's what helped

By Hamlin Rozario
May 21, 2026

Even though I've been using an RTX 4090 since 2022, I barely ever enabled frame generation for anything besides benchmarking. Every time I toggled it on, I was just underwhelmed with how the game felt while moving around, and turned it back off within minutes.
